name: Meta Platforms, Inc.
monetization: Monetizes AI through ad targeting/ranking and engagement across Facebook/Instagram/WhatsApp; no cloud business — AI is a cost center funded by ads, bonds, and off-balance-sheet SPVs.
description_md: Meta operates Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp and Messenger, funding one of the largest AI buildouts ($130–145B of 2026 capex) entirely from its advertising franchise — uniquely among the big four, it sells no cloud services, so AI spend has no direct compute-revenue offset. Meta pioneered the off-balance-sheet financing structures now spreading through the sector: the Hyperion JV in Louisiana (Blue Owl 80%/Meta 20%, $27B of A+ rated SPV notes anchored by PIMCO) and the El Paso venture (BlackRock 80%, $12.5B of bonds at 7.53%). It also rents third-party capacity at scale (CoreWeave ~$35B, Nebius up to $27B, Google Cloud >$10B) and bought 49% of Scale AI for $14.3B to seed its Superintelligence Labs.
ai_monetization_md: AI monetization is indirect: recommendation and ads models lift engagement and pricing across ~3.5B users, and generative ad tools raise advertiser spend — management attributes ad-revenue outperformance to AI ranking. There is no compute-resale revenue; Llama is open-weights and effectively unmonetized directly. The bet is that superintelligence-scale infrastructure (Hyperion ~5GW, Prometheus, El Paso 1GW) eventually monetizes through ads, agents, and devices. That makes Meta the sector's purest test of AI ROI without a cloud P&L: Q2-26 free cash flow fell to $0.78B (from $8.55B a year earlier) as capex consumed nearly all operating cash flow.
ai_strategy_md: Three-track capacity strategy: (1) **Own builds** funded on-balance-sheet — $130–145B 2026 capex plus a record $30B bond raise (Oct 2025, $125B of orders). (2) **SPV/JV structures** that move mega-campus capex off Meta's books while keeping operational control — Hyperion (Blue Owl 80/20, $27B notes, Meta took a ~$3B distribution and provides a residual-value guarantee) and El Paso (BlackRock 80/20, $12.5B at 7.53%). (3) **Rented neocloud capacity** — CoreWeave ~$35.2B through 2032, Nebius up to $27B, plus >$10B/6yr on Google Cloud. Talent/data via the $14.3B Scale AI deal (49%, non-voting) that brought Alexandr Wang in to lead Superintelligence Labs. Power via nuclear PPAs (Constellation Clinton 1,121MW; >2,600MW across Vistra's PJM fleet).
risk_notes_md: **SPV shift:** Hyperion and El Paso keep ~$40B+ of asset cost and debt off Meta's balance sheet while Meta retains use of the assets and (at Hyperion) a residual-value guarantee — the canonical spv_shift flag; where the risk truly sits is disclosed only partially. **Rising cost of capital:** El Paso's 7.53% (Jul 2026) vs Hyperion's A+ pricing a year earlier shows lenders repricing identical-sponsor risk; Morgan Stanley forecasts ~$570B of AI debt issuance in 2026 sector-wide. **FCF compression:** $0.78B Q2-26 FCF leaves the buyback/dividend and the capex plan competing for the same ad dollar; a digital-ad downturn transmits directly to the buildout. **No compute revenue offset:** unlike Azure/AWS/GCP, Meta cannot recycle AI capacity into third-party revenue if internal demand disappoints. **Commitment stack:** ~$62B of neocloud contracts (CoreWeave + Nebius) are firm obligations regardless of Llama's trajectory.

events.title: Forms Hyperion JV with Blue Owl (80/20); SPV issues $27B of A+ notes anchored by PIMCO ($18B)
events.why_it_matters: The template for off-balance-sheet AI financing: Meta's largest datacenter moves off its books, Meta takes a ~$3B distribution and provides a residual-value guarantee — the structure every credit analyst now stress-tests.

events.title: Sells $30B of bonds — its largest-ever offering — on $125B of orders
events.why_it_matters: Part of ~$121B of Big-5 2025 bond issuance; marks the AI trade's decisive move into the credit markets.

events.title: BlackRock raises $12.5B of bonds at 7.53% for the Meta El Paso SPV (BlackRock 80%/Meta 20%)
events.why_it_matters: Widest spread for an A-or-better rated bond in three years — visibly costlier than Hyperion, a live read on lenders repricing AI-datacenter risk.

events.title: Q2-26: free cash flow falls to $0.78B; 2026 capex floor raised to $130B
events.why_it_matters: The ad machine still grows, but cash generation net of AI capex approaches zero — the clearest single number on what the buildout costs an ads-only business model.
